title: Theme Parks in Korea for Families: Everland, Lotte World & More (2N3D Guide)
html:
Traveling with kids in Korea? You don't have to choose between temples and theme parks — Seoul has some of the biggest and most fun theme parks and aquariums in Asia, and most of them are an easy subway or bus ride from downtown. This guide gives you a simple 2-night, 3-day plan that mixes rides, animals, and sea creatures, plus a cheaper backup option if your budget is tight.

A quick note before you start: Korean amusement parks price tickets by date (busier days cost more) and change prices often, so treat every number below as a rough guide, not the final price. Always check the official website or app the week before you go.

Day 1 — Lotte World: Rides, a Lake, and a Mall All in One

Lotte World is in Jamsil, a neighborhood in southeast Seoul, right next to Jamsil Station (subway lines 2 and 8) — no long bus ride needed, which makes it the easiest first-day stop. It's actually two parks in one: Lotte World Adventure, a giant indoor hall full of rides, parades, and shows (great if it's raining or very cold), and Magic Island, an outdoor area built around a lake.

In April 2026, Lotte World opened a new permanent area on Magic Island called Maple Island, themed after the popular Korean video game MapleStory — it has new family-friendly rides and is a good spot for kids who like games and bright colors.

Opening hours are usually 10:00–21:00 Sunday–Thursday and 10:00–22:00 Friday–Saturday. Gate tickets for adults run around 64,000–67,000 KRW, but almost nobody pays that — see the tips section below.

Day 1 Extra — Lotte World Aquarium (Same Building)

If you still have energy after the rides, Lotte World Aquarium is inside the same Lotte World Mall complex, so you don't need to go anywhere else. It holds more than 55,000 sea animals, including a Beluga whale, and has a daily penguin-feeding show that young kids especially love.

It's open 10:00–20:00 (last entry 19:00). Online adult tickets are usually cheaper than paying at the door — expect somewhere in the 30,000–45,000 KRW range depending on where you book, so compare a couple of booking sites before buying.

Day 2 — Everland: Korea's Biggest Theme Park

Everland is Korea's largest theme park, about an hour outside Seoul in Yongin (Gyeonggi-do province). There's no subway station right at the gate, so the easiest way in is a direct shuttle bus from spots like Gangnam or Jamsil — Everland's own website lists current pickup points, or you can book a round-trip shuttle ticket through a travel app.

Everland is split into themed zones — Global Fair, American Adventure, Magic Land, European Adventure, and Zootopia — plus thrill rides like T-Express, Korea's first wooden roller coaster. If anyone in your group doesn't like fast rides, don't worry: most zones also have gentle, family-friendly attractions and shows.

Hours change by month, so check the Everland website before you go, but the park is usually open from around 10:00 until somewhere between 21:00 and 22:00.

Meet the Animals: Zootopia and Lost Valley

Inside Everland, Zootopia is a 15,000 m² zoo with about 2,000 animals, and it's one of the best parts of the park for younger children who might get tired of waiting in line for rides. Next to it, Lost Valley is a safari-style zone where you ride through in an open safari vehicle to see animals like lions and giraffes up close — book this one early in the day, since slots fill up fast.

💡 How locals actually do it: Korean visitors rarely buy the full-price ticket at the gate. Almost everyone books a discounted day pass in advance through a travel app (Klook, Trazy, Coupang, etc.) — it's the same ticket, just cheaper, and you skip the ticket-counter line completely.

Day 3 — COEX Aquarium in Gangnam (Easy Half-Day Stop)

For your last day, pick something light before heading to the airport or your next city. COEX Aquarium sits underneath the COEX Mall in Gangnam, right by Samseong Station (subway line 2), and holds around 40,000 sea creatures across 16 themed zones, including Korea's largest shark collection.

It's open 10:00–20:00 (last entry one hour before closing). Online adult tickets usually fall somewhere between 35,000–51,000 KRW depending on the booking site and current promotions — check a couple of sites, since prices move around a lot.

Because it's indoors and fully climate-controlled, it's also a smart backup plan if the weather turns bad on any of your three days.

On a Tight Budget? Try Seoulland Instead

If two big theme park days don't fit your budget or schedule, Seoulland is a smaller, cheaper alternative in Gwacheon, just south of Seoul, inside the larger Seoul Grand Park area (which also has a zoo and a cable car up the mountain). Ticket prices are noticeably lower than Everland or Lotte World — often under 20,000 KRW for foreign-visitor tickets booked online, and there's also a cheaper evening ticket (sometimes called "After 6") if you only want a few hours.

Hours are usually 10:00–19:00 on weekdays and a bit later on weekends, but double-check before visiting since Seoulland adjusts hours by season.

Tips for Visiting With Kids

  • Buy tickets online, not at the gate. It's almost always cheaper and skips the line — this is true for every park and aquarium in this guide.
  • Download the park's app before you go (Everland and Lotte World both have one). At Everland, the free Smart Queue feature lets you reserve a return time for popular rides instead of standing in a physical line — but it usually stops working around 14:00, and popular rides like T-Express can fill up by late morning, so reserve your must-do rides as soon as you arrive.
  • Go on a weekday if you can. Weekends and Korean public holidays get very crowded, especially at Everland and Lotte World.
  • Bring a light jacket for aquariums. Both COEX Aquarium and Lotte World Aquarium keep the halls cool.
  • Carry small cash or a card for lockers and snacks. Most rides have free lockers near the entrance, but some need a small coin deposit.

Which Park Should You Pick?

Park Typical Online Price (Adult) Travel Time from Seoul Best For
Everland ~39,000–45,000 KRW ~1 hour (shuttle bus) Biggest rides, full day out, zoo + safari
Lotte World ~38,000–45,000 KRW 5 min walk from Jamsil Station Rainy days, no long travel, aquarium nearby
Seoulland ~15,000–20,000 KRW ~40 min (subway + shuttle) Tight budgets, shorter visits, evening tickets

💬 Got a question about which park fits your trip best? Drop it in the comments below — happy to help you plan!
meta_description: A 2-night, 3-day plan for Everland, Lotte World, two aquariums, and a budget-friendly backup park, with prices, hours, and kid tips.
